title: Memory in Time: A Network Model of Information Aging and a Strategy for Constructing Retrospective Databases
affiliations: National Technical University of Ukraine - Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute and A&I, Tata Consultancy Services

detail.title: Memory in Time: A Network Model of Information Aging and a Strategy for Constructing Retrospective Databases
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a conception of memory as a dynamic projection of an event network, in which time emerges not as an absolute quantity but as a partial order induced by causal relationships. Building on this foundation, we develop a network model of information aging that distinguishes between ephemeral (news-like) and stable (encyclopedic) information, yet focuses not on the events themselves but on their topological roles-particularly the preservation of-bridges‖ that connect historical-anchors.‖ We introduce a filtering strategy for large-scale archives (30 years, over one billion records) that minimizes the volume of readily accessible storage without compromising the integrity of causal chains. The model is formalized through a cryptographic analogy involving archetypal agents-Alice (human memory), Bob (the archive), and Eve (erroneous reconstruction)enabling the identification and avoidance of-real-time‖ paradoxes arising when associative links supplant causal ones. The result is a practical archival policy that preserves not-everything,‖ but only what sustains meaning.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种将记忆视为事件网络动态投影的概念，其中时间不是绝对量而是由因果关系诱导的偏序关系。基于此，我们开发了一个信息老化网络模型，区分短暂（新闻类）和稳定（百科类）信息，但关注的是事件的拓扑角色——特别是连接历史“锚点”的“桥梁”的保存。我们引入了一种大规模档案（30年，超过10亿条记录）的过滤策略，在不损害因果链完整性的前提下最小化易访问存储量。该模型通过密码学类比（Alice代表人类记忆，Bob代表档案，Eve代表错误重构）形式化，能够识别和避免当关联链接取代因果链接时出现的“实时”悖论。结果是制定了一个实用的档案策略，不是“保存一切”，而是只保存维持意义的内容。
AI.research_question: 如何在大规模档案中设计有效的过滤策略，既最小化存储需求又保持因果链的完整性？
AI.motivation: 传统档案方法倾向于保存所有信息，导致存储成本高昂且信息过载。需要一种更智能的方法来区分哪些信息真正值得保存以维持历史意义。
AI.theoretical_framework: 记忆作为事件网络的动态投影理论；时间作为因果关系诱导的偏序关系；信息老化的网络模型；拓扑角色分析（桥梁与锚点）；密码学类比框架
AI.method: 开发网络模型区分短暂与稳定信息；引入基于拓扑角色的过滤策略；使用密码学类比形式化模型（Alice、Bob、Eve）；在大规模档案数据集（30年，10亿+记录）上验证
AI.findings: 提出的过滤策略能够显著减少存储需求而不损害因果完整性；拓扑角色分析有助于识别关键信息节点；密码学框架有效避免了实时悖论
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了记忆作为事件网络动态投影的新概念；发展了基于拓扑角色的信息老化理论；建立了档案管理的密码学类比框架
AI.practical_contributions: 提供了实用的档案过滤策略；为大规模信息管理提供了可操作的解决方案；帮助组织更有效地管理历史档案

detail.title: Sentiment Analysis towards Influencer Marketing in the Food Industry

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no conflict of interest for this work. There are also no personal, financial or professional relationships that could have influenced the outcome of this research in any way.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Qualitative interviews and focus group discussions were held with industry experts, content creators and consumers for this study. The study complies to ethical research norms of voluntary participation, anonymity and confidentiality. detail.abstract: Purpose-Recently social media influencer marketing has been evolved over the time, especially in the food industry. But sentiments towards the influencer are not fully trusted among the consumers. Thus, this paper aims to investigate the sentiment towards influencer marketing on the purchase intention of consumers in the food industry. Design/methodology/approach-It is a qualitative research approach used for conducting this study. Influencer marketing was evaluated using sentiment analysis regarding consumer reactions. Sixty-five participants were asked about their attitudes and feelings towards influencer contents in the food industry. An in-depth interview was conducted to get insights into the sentiment towards the influencer marketing. Findings-The study shows that most of the participants offered negative feedback because of their beliefs about false reviews and paid advertisements. While some respondents said they could gain information from influencer contents, it was only sometimes a complete buying decision. A smaller number expressed positive feelings, acknowledging influencer content's creativity and convenience aspects. The attitudes, perceived credibility, and choice influence arising from influencer-generated contents are identified in this study based on data gained from 65 study participants. Practical Implications-The study emphasizes the importance of implementing authentic and transparent influencer marketing methods to regain the consumers' belief. The study's conclusion entails suggestions on how food brands can enhance the effectiveness of influencer marketing through credibility apprehensions, sentiment analysis regarding the customers' expectations. Consequently, this research offers vital information regarding the significant impact of influencer marketing on consumer behavior in today's ever-competing food industry. Originality/value-This study aims to explore insights about the effect of influencer marketing on consumer purchasing behavior within the fast and competitive food sector. This paper demonstrates the importance of sentiment analysis in selecting the celebrity for influencer marketing and provides suggestions for enhancing the believability of influencers and customers' interactions.

title: ISO 27001 and Alternative Frameworks for Managing Information Security Risks
affiliations: University of the Cumberlands (formerly Cumberland College)

detail.title: ISO 27001 and Alternative Frameworks for Managing Information Security Risks
detail.abstract: Information security risks increasingly threaten organizational resilience, eroding operational continuity, reputational capital, and long-term enterprise value. To address these risks, organizations adopt international frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001, COBIT, ITIL, OCTAVE, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF). This paper critically examines ISO 27001 as a baseline for Information Security Management Systems (ISMS), assessing its effectiveness and limitations within the context of financial services. While ISO 27001 provides global recognition, certification credibility, and structured governance, it is often undermined by high implementation costs, resource demands, and the risk of "checklist compliance." A comparative analysis highlights complementary frameworks, COBIT for IT governance, OCTAVE for rigorous risk assessment, NIST CSF for adaptive resilience, and SOC 2 for cloud assurance, which address gaps left unfulfilled by ISO 27001. The findings underscore that hybrid adoption models are superior, as they align security controls with enterprise risk management (ERM) principles, such as integration, risk appetite alignment, and continuous improvement. The paper concludes that reframing information security as a strategic component of ERM, supported by hybrid frameworks and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, enables organizations to move beyond compliance toward predictive, adaptive, and value-creating risk management.

AI.tldr: 本文批判性分析ISO 27001作为信息安全管理系统基准的有效性和局限性，指出混合采用模型结合COBIT、OCTAVE、NIST CSF等框架更优，建议将信息安全重构为企业风险管理的战略组成部分。
AI.research_question: ISO 27001作为信息安全管理系统基准在金融服务环境中的有效性和局限性是什么？
AI.motivation: 信息安全风险日益威胁组织韧性，侵蚀运营连续性、声誉资本和长期企业价值，需要评估现有国际框架的有效性。
AI.theoretical_framework: 企业风险管理(ERM)原则，包括整合、风险偏好对齐和持续改进。
AI.method: 比较分析，评估ISO 27001与其他框架(COBIT、OCTAVE、NIST CSF、SOC 2)的互补性。
AI.findings: ISO 27001具有全球认可和结构化治理优势，但存在高实施成本、资源需求和"清单合规"风险；混合采用模型更优。
AI.theory_contributions: 将信息安全重构为企业风险管理的战略组成部分，提出基于混合框架的预测性、适应性和价值创造型风险管理理论。
AI.practical_contributions: 为组织提供混合框架采用策略，帮助从合规导向转向价值创造型风险管理，支持人工智能等新兴技术的应用。

title: Unequal Transmission: Monetary Policy and Household Consumption in India
affiliations: Hamilton College and

detail.title: Unequal Transmission: Monetary Policy and Household Consumption in India
detail.abstract: This paper provides new empirical evidence on the effects of monetary policy shocks on household consumption, income, and employment in a large developing economy. Using high-frequency identification of monetary surprises combined with local projection methods, we estimate dynamic impulse responses to both current and expected policy shocks. Our results indicate that a contractionary shock to the short-term policy rate raises consumption and income on impact but reduces them in the medium run, while employment declines persistently. In contrast, a contractionary shock to the expected path of future interest rates increase consumption and employment but lowers income. The effects are stronger after the first quarter, suggesting delayed transmission. We also observe heterogeneity across socioeconomic groups: rural households, those with lower education, women, younger and older workers, and lower-caste groups exhibit significantly larger consumption declines. A back-of-the-envelope calculation yields a marginal propensity to consume of about 40 percent out of transitory, policy induced income changes. Our findings highlight the importance of distributional channels in shaping the aggregate transmission of monetary policy in developing economies.

title: The Impact of China's Digital Financial Inclusion on Multidimensional Poverty of Households​
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics and Tsinghua University

detail.title: The Impact of China's Digital Financial Inclusion on Multidimensional Poverty of Households​
detail.abstract: Does digital financial inclusion alleviate poverty? This study investigates this question by integrating the Digital Financial Inclusion Index of Peking University with microdata from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) to examine how the expansion of digital financial inclusion affects household multidimensional poverty in China. Anchored in Amartya Sen’s capability approach and operationalized through the Alkire–Foster (A–F) framework, the study identifies multidimensional poverty across five key dimensions: income, health, education, insurance, and living standards. Probit models are employed to estimate how digital financial inclusion influences both the likelihood and structure of multidimensional poverty, while instrumental variable techniques are used to address potential endogeneity. Beyond the average effects, the study further explores the mechanisms through which digital financial inclusion contributes to poverty alleviation, focusing on three channels—promoting household consumption, increasing financial investment, and enhancing access to credit. The results reveal that digital financial inclusion significantly mitigates multidimensional poverty, particularly by improving income, living standards, and health outcomes, though its effects on education and insurance are limited. These findings underscore the transformative role of digital finance in fostering inclusive growth, suggesting that policies expanding digital financial infrastructure and literacy can amplify its poverty-reducing effects and advance equitable development.

AI.tldr: 本研究探讨数字普惠金融是否缓解贫困，通过整合北京大学数字普惠金融指数与中国家庭追踪调查(CFPS)微观数据，基于Sen的能力方法和Alkire-Foster框架分析数字普惠金融对中国家庭多维贫困的影响。研究发现数字普惠金融显著减轻多维贫困，主要通过改善收入、生活水平和健康状况，但对教育和保险影响有限。

title: Navigating the Approaching Tide: Financial Stocks for Resilience in an NPA-Laden Environment
affiliations: IGNOU

detail.title: Navigating the Approaching Tide: Financial Stocks for Resilience in an NPA-Laden Environment
detail.abstract: The mounting shadow of non-performing assets (NPAs) continues to shape the contours of financial stability across global and domestic markets. As the Indian economy enters a phase of cyclical credit recalibration under the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2025, investors are compelled to reevaluate their strategies for resilience and sustainable returns. This paper examines the dynamic interplay between credit risk, macroeconomic stress, and institutional adaptability, identifying key categories of financial entities banks, fintechs, and asset reconstruction companies (ARCs) that exhibit structural resilience amid escalating NPA cycles. Drawing on historical patterns from the Global Financial Crisis (2008), the Indian credit stress era (2012-2017), and post-pandemic adjustments (2020-2025), this study synthesizes empirical evidence, policy frameworks, and sectoral data to construct a Resilience Matrix for investors. The findings reveal that financial institutions with diversified revenue models, high Capital Adequacy Ratios (CARs), strong provisioning practices, and agile technological risk-mitigation mechanisms are more likely to outperform in an NPA-laden environment. The paper also highlights how fintech debt-resolution models, AI-based credit scoring, and regulatory convergence are redefining the future of NPA management. Ultimately, this research seeks to humanize investment strategy by illustrating how rational risk assessment, disciplined capital management, and adaptive innovation can collectively navigate the approaching tide of NPAs while preserving both shareholder value and systemic stability.

title: Navigating Workers' Data Rights in the Digital Age: A Historical, Current, and Future Perspective on Workers' Data Protection
affiliations: Utrecht University - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Navigating Workers' Data Rights in the Digital Age: A Historical, Current, and Future Perspective on Workers' Data Protection
detail.abstract:
Over recent decades, comprehensive data protection legislation has proliferated worldwide, with a majority of jurisdictions enacting robust statutory regimes. Despite this abundance of legal standards, persistent challenges remain regarding the efficacy of these laws in protecting individuals‒ particularly workers‒within the increasingly digitalised workplace. Workers are especially susceptible to harm due to entrenched power asymmetries and heightened risks of data exploitation, yet many existing legal frameworks provide insufficient or inconsistent protection, and some jurisdictions explicitly exclude workers from coverage.

This research critically examines the multidimensional risks associated with workplace digitalisation and systematically analyses regulatory challenges and protection gaps across diverse jurisdictions. By integrating historical analysis, current policy initiatives, and comparative cross-jurisdictional perspectives, the study identifies structural deficiencies in prevailing approaches. It concludes by proposing policy solutions to advance worker-centric data governance frameworks, tailored to address the distinctive challenges of contemporary labour relations and to ensure more equitable and effective protection for workers in the digital age.

AI.tldr: 本文批判性分析了工作场所数字化带来的多维风险，系统性地比较了不同司法管辖区的监管挑战和保护差距，并提出以工人为中心的数据治理框架政策解决方案。

title: Do Banks Trade on Private Information? Evidence from Bank-Insurer CDS Trading
affiliations: Fordham University  , University of California, Irvine - Paul Merage School of Business, Bowling Green State University - College of Business Administration and

detail.title: Do Banks Trade on Private Information? Evidence from Bank-Insurer CDS Trading
detail.abstract: Banks acquire privileged borrower information through lending. By matching loan and CDS data, we provide transaction-level evidence that banks purchasing credit default swap (CDS) contracts on their borrowers predict notable CDS spread widening across short and long horizons, as well as negative rating actions. The effect intensifies for lead arrangers with larger exposures, stricter covenants, opaque borrowers, and ahead of major credit events, revealing a systematic channel where privileged information enables profitable CDS trades. Our findings extend prior research—focused on equities or non-bank participants — to banks in the derivatives market, with significant implications for bank oversight and CDS regulation.

title: Silence as a Social Equilibrium: A Graph-Domination Model of Recognition Asymmetry
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Silence as a Social Equilibrium: A Graph-Domination Model of Recognition Asymmetry

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper reconceptualizes silence not as an individual pathology or communication breakdown but as a rationally emergent social equilibrium. Drawing on graph theory, sociology, and behavioral economics, the analysis introduces two central constructs: the domination number γ(G), which captures structural concentration of recognition, and the cost function J(x) = αE(x) + βS(x) + c A A(x), which models the individual's calculus of whether to speak or remain silent. Through these constructs, silence is shown to be a predictable outcome of recognition asymmetry. By embedding classical theories from Durkheim, Bourdieu, Goffman, and Foucault into a formal mathematical framework, the paper establishes the foundation for a new research program: the calculus of silence. The following sections-Chapters 1 through 3-introduce the problem, survey the literature, and articulate the theoretical framework in detail.

AI.tldr: 本文重新概念化沉默，将其视为理性出现的社会均衡而非个体病理或沟通障碍。通过图论、社会学和行为经济学，引入支配数γ(G)和成本函数J(x)来建模沉默行为，证明沉默是认可不对称的可预测结果。
AI.research_question: 沉默如何作为理性社会均衡出现？认可不对称如何影响个体选择沉默的决策？
AI.motivation: 传统研究将沉默视为个体病理或沟通失败，但本文认为沉默是理性社会互动的可预测结果，需要新的理论框架来解释。
AI.theoretical_framework: 图论（支配数γ(G)）、行为经济学（成本函数J(x)）、社会学理论（涂尔干、布迪厄、戈夫曼、福柯的经典理论）
AI.method: 理论建模方法，结合数学形式化框架和社会学理论分析
AI.findings: 沉默是认可不对称的可预测结果，支配数γ(G)捕捉认可的结构集中度，成本函数J(x)建模个体说话或沉默的决策计算
AI.theory_contributions: 建立了"沉默计算"研究计划，将经典社会学理论嵌入数学框架，为沉默研究提供新的理论基础
AI.practical_contributions: 为理解组织、社会群体中的沉默现象提供分析工具，帮助识别和解决认可不对称问题

title: The Term Structure of Stock-Bond Covariances

detail.title: The Term Structure of Stock-Bond Covariances
detail.abstract: I study the term structure of stock-bond covariances after the Global Financial Crisis. The term structure of covariances refers to the covariance between the aggregate market and government bonds of different maturities. I establish five new facts about the term structure of covariances: (1) The average term structure of covariances is downward sloping: long-maturity covariances are more negative than their short-maturity counterparts, whereas the term structure is flat across maturities before the crisis. (2) After the crisis, short-maturity covariances are acyclical. Short-maturity covariances are of the same magnitude in good and bad times, and so are acyclical. In contrast, long-maturity covariances are more negative in bad times, and so are countercyclical. Taken together, the first two facts imply that short-maturity bonds have weaker hedging properties relative to long-maturity bonds. (3) To generalize the intuition from the first two facts, I run regressions of long-maturity covariances on short-maturity covariances in changes. Before 2007, the sensitivity of long to short, the regression slope, is about one and stable. After 2010, the sensitivity roughly doubles. (4) The sensitivity of long to short is related to unconventional monetary policy. First, in the United States, the sensitivity rises only after the announcement of largescale asset purchases and varies with Post-GFC programs implemented by the Federal Reserve. Second, around the world, the rise in the sensitivity is larger in countries with larger quantitative easing programs. (5) The break in the term structure has implications for bond risk premia. I construct a stock-bond factor, analogous to the Cochrane-Piazzesi factor, from the term structure of covariances. After the crisis but not before, the stock-bond factor predicts bond excess returns, even after controlling for typical predictors of bond returns. These five facts provide new directions for the literature on stock-bond comovement.

title: Relating Integer Programs: An Experimental Study on the State of the Art
affiliations: State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo, University at Buffalo (SUNY) - School of Management and State University of New York (SUNY) - University at Buffalo

detail.title: Relating Integer Programs: An Experimental Study on the State of the Art
detail.abstract: Integer linear programs (ILPs) are a foundational modeling tool in operations research, yet their mathematical structure complicates efforts to relate instances. Recent work has proposed surrogate representations to regularize ILPs into forms amenable to vectorization and learning, including a tabular-based (TCIP), image-based (ICIP), and graph-based (GCIP) approach. This paper presents the first systematic computational study of these approaches. Using 1,240 ILP instances from the strIPlib library spanning 23 problem classes (e.g., bin packing, lot sizing, etc.) and multiple formulations within classes, we robustly evaluate each representation in two tasks: unsupervised instance comparison and supervised classification. For comparison, we assess match rates, clustering performance, and principal component analyses. For classification, we introduce an integer program that generates structurally diverse train-test splits to mitigate overfitting. We then benchmark a range of learning models, presenting the first application of TCIP features in ILP classification, and the first use of GCIP features outside the framework of graph-based machine learning models. Our results show that GCIP consistently achieves superior structural discrimination, while TCIP performs competitively in supervised classification settings. The collective findings establish a comparative baseline for ILP representation methods and present new techniques and findings that significantly augment advance knowledge in relating ILPs.

AI.tldr: 本文对三种整数线性规划表示方法（TCIP、ICIP、GCIP）进行了系统评估，发现在结构区分方面GCIP表现最佳，在监督分类中TCIP表现竞争性。
AI.research_question: 如何系统地评估和比较不同的整数线性规划表示方法在实例比较和分类任务中的性能？
AI.motivation: 整数线性规划是运筹学中的基础建模工具，但其数学结构使得实例间关系分析变得复杂，需要系统评估现有表示方法的有效性。

AI.findings: GCIP在结构区分方面表现最优，TCIP在监督分类任务中表现竞争性，ICIP整体表现相对较弱。
AI.theory_contributions: 建立了ILP表示方法的比较基准，提出了生成结构多样化训练测试分割的整数规划方法。
AI.practical_contributions: 为ILP实例分析和分类提供了实用的表示方法选择指导，首次将TCIP特征应用于ILP分类，首次在非图机器学习模型中使用GCIP特征。

title: An Evolutionary Analysis of Narrative Selection
affiliations: University of Verona and University of Siena

detail.title: An Evolutionary Analysis of Narrative Selection
detail.abstract: We study the performance of different methods for processing information, incorporating narrative selection within an evolutionary model. All agents update their beliefs according to Bayes' Rule, but some strategically choose the narrative they use in updating according to heterogeneous criteria. We simulate the endogenous composition of the population, considering different laws of motion for the underlying state of the world. We find that conformists-that is, agents that choose the narrative to conform to the average belief in the population-have an evolutionary advantage over other agents across all specifications. The survival chances of the remaining types depend on the uncertainty regarding the state of the world. Agents who tend to develop mild beliefs perform better when the uncertainty is high, whereas agents who tend to develop extreme beliefs perform better when the uncertainty is low.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了在进化模型中不同信息处理方法的表现，重点关注叙事选择。所有代理都根据贝叶斯规则更新信念，但有些代理根据异质标准战略性地选择用于更新的叙事。研究发现，在所有规范中，从众者（选择叙事以符合群体平均信念的代理）比其他代理具有进化优势。其他类型的生存机会取决于世界状态的不确定性程度。

AI.theoretical_framework: 进化模型、贝叶斯信念更新、叙事选择理论、从众行为理论

title: Extending Employee Compensation Schemes to the Informal Economy: Policy Frameworks, Innovations, and Implementation Challenges
affiliations: ACTAG

detail.title: Extending Employee Compensation Schemes to the Informal Economy: Policy Frameworks, Innovations, and Implementation Challenges
detail.abstract: The informal economy employs approximately 2 billion workers globally, representing 61.2% of the world's employed population, yet the majority lack access to employee compensation and social protection schemes. This paper examines the current status of compensation schemes across formal and informal economies, analyzes successful implementation models, and proposes evidence-based frameworks for extending coverage. Through comparative case study analysis of policy developments in Nigeria, Uruguay, Brazil, and India, alongside international frameworks such as ILO Recommendation 204, this study identifies critical success factors, implementation challenges, and risk mitigation strategies. The research contributes to academic discourse by synthesizing emerging innovations in adaptive social protection and digital platform integration while addressing the structural barriers that perpetuate exclusion of informal workers from social security systems. Methodologically, the study employs systematic literature review combined with policy document analysis and case study comparison to develop actionable recommendations for policymakers and practitioners.

title: Estimation and Inference for Unbalanced Panel Data Models with Interactive Fixed Effects
affiliations: Tsinghua University, Peking University - School of Economics and Hunan University

detail.title: Estimation and Inference for Unbalanced Panel Data Models with Interactive Fixed Effects
detail.abstract: This paper establishes the inferential theory for unbalanced panel data models with interactive fixed effects. We propose a two-step estimation algorithm with the first step obtaining an initial consistent estimator followed by an alternating maximization procedure. We prove that the alternating maximization procedure is a contractionary mapping and the final estimator is asymptotically normal, as long as the initial estimator is consistent. We also develop analytical bias corrections according to the derived asymptotic bias expressions and the observed missing pattern. Our results cover important missing patterns such as completely exogenous missing, selection on regressors/factors/loadings and block/staggered missing, and we also show that our results can be readily extended to cases with a Heckman correction term or more general settings. An empirical analysis of the U.S. state-level tax rates from 1951 to 2000 with missing data reveals persistence in tax rates, while state income influences different taxes in varying ways.

title: Territorialized Security-by-Design: Integrating Perceptions, Freight Fluidity Approach, and Physical Internet to Reduce Cargo Theft Risks
affiliations: , Texas A&M International University and Texas A&M International University

detail.title: Territorialized Security-by-Design: Integrating Perceptions, Freight Fluidity Approach, and Physical Internet to Reduce Cargo Theft Risks
detail.abstract: Cargo theft represents a rising threat to international business, eroding supply chain reliability, consumer trust, and global trade stability. This paper advances Territorialized Security-by-Design as an integrative framework for proactively addressing these risks. The approach combines three critical dimensions: (i) human perceptions of safety that shape freight routing decisions, (ii) vulnerabilities linked to cross-border freight fluidity in risk corridors, and (iii) technological innovations inspired by the Physical Internet (π) that enable modular and theft-resilient transportation systems. By integrating behavioral insights with advanced logistical architectures, this framework transcends reactive security measures to embed resilience directly into the design of logistics networks. For global decision-makers, the key insight is that perceptions of insecurity are not marginal; they actively redirect trade flows, increase dwell times, and heighten exposure to theft. Consequently, effective strategies must integrate socio-geographical risk awareness with modular, digitally secure, and interoperable infrastructure. The paper outlines a practitioner agenda for policymakers and business leaders, emphasizing the importance of cross-border collaboration, cyber-physical resilience, and proactive risk governance. Ultimately, Territorialized Security-by-Design reframes cargo theft not as an isolated criminal issue, but as a systemic international business challenge that requires coordinated, design-driven responses across the physical, human, and digital dimensions of the supply chain.

title: Spackling Uncertainty with Flexibility in Operating Room Capacity Allocation
affiliations: Aalto University, Aalto University - School of Science, , KU Leuven, Helsinki University Hospital, Helsinki University Hospital and Helsinki University

detail.title: Spackling Uncertainty with Flexibility in Operating Room Capacity Allocation
detail.abstract: Effective operating room (OR) capacity planning is essential for balancing patient care quality with healthcare system efficiency. Traditional planning approaches often struggle to accommodate unpredictable emergency (EM) surgeries alongside scheduled elective (EL) cases, leading to costly inefficiencies such as overtime and undertime. This study tactically categorizes surgeries into high (EM), moderate (general elective, GE), and low (flexible elective, FE) volatility to create a volatility portfolio that strategically spackles unused capacity and absorbs demand fluctuations, while ensuring that a stable number of ELs can be processed reliably despite uncertainty. Using an explorative design science research (DSR) approach, it embeds demand-side flexibility to buffer against uncertainty in surgical demand. Through collaboration with hospitals, we first frame and conceptualize the challenges of OR capacity allocation, and a critical assessment of existing methods reveals significant opportunities for more adaptive and efficient planning. Next, empirical data show that our approach with 10-20% flexibility can substantially improve OR utilization from 60% to 90% and reduce overtime by 20%, with its effectiveness further confirmed through simulation experiments and sensitivity analyses. Finally, practitioner validation workshops assess feasibility, adaptability, and potential for broader application of our proposed approach in healthcare and other capacity-constrained settings.

title: Selection into Tariff Avoidance and the Measured Welfare Cost of Tariffs
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

detail.title: Selection into Tariff Avoidance and the Measured Welfare Cost of Tariffs
detail.abstract: Standard estimates suggest U.S. importers bear the full incidence of tariffs. I show these estimates are biased upwards because low-passthrough exporters are more likely to select into avoidance behavior. Namely, these exporters avoid tariffs by rerouting exports through countries facing lower tariffs---transshipping---leaving only high-passthrough firms directly exporting to the U.S. I exploit variation in exposure to the U.S.-China trade war to estimate both intensive and extensive elasticities of transshipment. I find that a ten percentage point increase in the tariff rate increases the probability of transshipment by 10-30 percentage points and increases the share of transshipped goods by 2-11 percentage points. The effects are entirely concentrated in intermediate and capital goods, with no apparent behavioral response from consumption goods. My empirical results imply that the lower bound on estimated U.S. incidence is 85 percent, raising the possibility that some types of tariffs are no more costly on the margin than lump-sum taxes. Finally, I identify a novel channel through which domestic tax policy implicitly deters international tax avoidance. Because import costs are tax-deductible, higher corporate tax rates discourage transshipping. For that reason, the 2017 corporate tax cuts increased transshipping, costing the U.S. $2-$9 billion in tariff revenue.

AI.tldr: 本文研究发现传统关税承担率估计存在向上偏差，因为低转嫁率的出口商会通过转运来规避关税。基于中美贸易战数据，发现关税每增加10个百分点，转运概率增加10-30个百分点，转运商品份额增加2-11个百分点。这些效应完全集中在中间品和资本品上。研究还发现公司税率降低会鼓励转运行为，2017年减税导致美国损失20-90亿美元关税收入。

title: The Use of Open-Source Software by Library Users in Some Private Universities in Ghana

detail.title: The Use of Open-Source Software by Library Users in Some Private Universities in Ghana
detail.abstract: Introduction: this study explores the use of open-source software (OSS) by library users at Pentecost University (PU) and Central University (CU) with a focus on the ease of use, and barriers encountered. This study adopted the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) as its framework. Method: a descriptive survey design was employed and targeting registered undergraduate library users at both institutions. Result: 134 PU library users (88,2 %) indicated that unstable internet connectivity on campus is a significant barrier to using open-source software in the Pentecost University library. Concerning library users in Central University (CU), 120 respondents (90,2 %) indicated that the lack of support and training is a significant barrier hindering the use of open-source software in the Central University library. Conclusion: the study identified a divergence in the frequency of use, with CU users engaging with opensource software daily, while PU users employed it several times a week. Both CU and PU users found opensource software easy to use and interact with, contributing to a positive user experience. User-friendliness emerged as a critical factor influencing the extent of open-source software adoption. The study identified barriers that impede the effective use of open-source software, including unreliable internet connectivity at PU and inadequate resources in support and training at CU. Hence, the library administration should adopt strategies and regulations to address the difficulties faced when utilising Open-Source Software, such as providing guidance, assistance, and instructional resources.

AI.tldr: 本研究基于技术接受模型，调查了Pentecost大学和Central大学图书馆用户使用开源软件的情况。研究发现两校用户都认为开源软件易用，但面临不同障碍：PU大学主要是网络连接不稳定，CU大学则是缺乏支持培训。
AI.research_question: Pentecost大学和Central大学图书馆用户使用开源软件的易用性和障碍是什么？
AI.motivation: 探索开源软件在高校图书馆中的使用情况，识别影响用户采用的关键因素和障碍
AI.theoretical_framework: 技术接受模型（TAM）
AI.method: 描述性调查研究，针对两所大学的注册本科图书馆用户
AI.findings: PU大学88.2%用户认为网络不稳定是主要障碍，CU大学90.2%用户认为缺乏支持培训是主要障碍；CU用户每天使用开源软件，PU用户每周使用数次；两校用户都认为开源软件易用
AI.theory_contributions: 验证了技术接受模型在开源软件应用情境下的适用性，扩展了该模型在图书馆环境中的应用

title: Legal and Policy Pathways to Combat Gas Flaring toward Net-Zero Emissions in Nigeria
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Legal and Policy Pathways to Combat Gas Flaring toward Net-Zero Emissions in Nigeria
detail.abstract:
Nigeria continues to be one of the leading nations globally in gas flaring.  A 2022 report estimated that approximately 50% of the country's annual gas production is flared.  Despite numerous regulatory initiatives, the practice persists, discharging millions of tons of carbon dioxide, methane, and other harmful substances into the atmosphere. Nigeria's share of global gas flaring increased by 12 % in 2024, reflecting non-compliance with existing regulations. Such actions adversely affect the country's international standing regarding environmental protection and undermine its commitments under the Paris Agreement and the 2050 net-zero emissions targets. Given the substantial emissions of greenhouse gases (GHG) resulting from flaring, this practice constitute a significant environmental concern within the global initiative to limit temperature increases below 2°C above pre-industrial levels , with an aspirational target of 1.5°C. In Nigeria, gas flaring has worsened severe environmental and public health challenges, contributed to energy insecurity, and promoted the unsustainable exploitation of natural resources.

This paper assesses the legal, policy, financial, and infrastructural deficiencies that sustain gas flaring in Nigeria. It contextualises Nigeria's anti-flaring initiatives within the broader framework of international environmental law. It provides a strategic roadmap for reform to eliminate flaring by 2030 and support the country in attaining its net-zero emissions goal.

title: Why Tax Cuts Don't Boost Capital as Much as We Predict: The Maintenance Margin
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

detail.title: Why Tax Cuts Don't Boost Capital as Much as We Predict: The Maintenance Margin
detail.abstract: I show that standard models overstate how much business tax cuts boost capital accumulation because they treat the demand for capital maintenance as exogenously zero. Firms adjust the capital stock through investment in new assets and maintenance of old ones, but tax law treats these margins differently. Accounting for maintenance attenuates the effects of tax cuts through two channels. First is a tax shield effect: tax cuts reduce the tax savings from maintenance deductions, so the effective cost of capital falls by less than standard models predict. Second is an input substitution effect: tax cuts make new investment relatively cheaper, causing firms to substitute away from maintenance, which makes capital depreciate more quickly. Both channels depend on the level and elasticity of maintenance demand, which I estimate using digitized Class I railroad filings and IRS industry data. In general equilibrium, I find that accounting for maintenance implies the effects of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on capital, output, and wages are about one-third smaller than standard estimates---approximately $240 billion less corporate capital after ten years than an equivalent model without maintenance would predict.

title: Equity Volatility Persistence and Leverage Adjustment Speed
affiliations: ESADE Business School, Ramon Llull University and EADA Business School

detail.title: Equity Volatility Persistence and Leverage Adjustment Speed
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first empirical test, and confirmation, of the hypothesis that the slow adjustment of firms toward their target leverage ratios underlies the greater persistence of equity volatility relative to asset volatility (Choi and Richardson, 2016). In the time series, and consistent with this hypothesis, we find that the difference between equity and asset volatility persistence varies with macroeconomic conditions, widening during crisis periods. In the cross section, firm-specific factors identified in the literature as affecting the speed of leverage adjustment also help explain this difference. Overall, our results support the view that the greater the flexibility firms have to adjust their leverage ratios, the lower the persistence of equity volatility relative to asset volatility.

title: From Constraints to Rational Preferences

detail.title: From Constraints to Rational Preferences

publicationDetails.detailsText: This paper previously circulated with the title: "Incorporating Sustainability into Portfolio Choices: A Rational Investor Approach"

detail.abstract: Standard approaches to portfolio optimization often rely on constraints to proxy investor preferences, assuming equivalence with utility-based formulations. This paper challenges that assumption by developing a general framework that characterizes conditions under which constraints can rationalize preferences. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for equivalence, revealing that constraints can misrepresent investor behavior or overlook heterogeneity. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-objective optimization framework that allows trade-offs to be determined endogenously rather than fixed ex ante. We extend the classical mean-variance model to sustainable investing, and derive closed-form equilibrium strategies in complete markets. Using simulations and U.S. equity data, we construct a three-dimensional mean-variancesustainability efficient frontier that captures the trade-offs among the different objectives. Our framework offers a flexible foundation for portfolio design and sustainable investing, with practical relevance for asset managers and policymakers.

title: The Measurement of Profit, Profitability, Cost and Revenue Efficiency through Data Envelopment Analysis: A Comparison of Models using BenchmarkingEconomicEfficiency.jl
affiliations: Universidad Autónoma de Madrid and Universidad Autónoma de Madrid

detail.title: The Measurement of Profit, Profitability, Cost and Revenue Efficiency through Data Envelopment Analysis: A Comparison of Models using BenchmarkingEconomicEfficiency.jl

contentType.other: An abridged version of this WP has been published in an article with the same title

detail.abstract: We undertake a systematic comparison of existing models measuring and decomposing the economic efficiency of organizations. For this purpose we introduce the package BenchmarkingEconomicEfficiency.jl for the open-source Julia language including a set of functions to be used by scholars and professionals working in the fields of economics, management science, engineering, and operations research. Using mathematical programming methods known as Data Envelopment Analysis, the software develops code to decompose economic efficiency considering alternative definitions: profit, profitability, cost and revenue. Economic efficiency can be decomposed, multiplicative or additively, into a technical (productive) efficiency term and a residual term representing allocative (or price) efficiency. We include traditional decompositions like the radial efficiency measures associated with the input (cost) and output (revenue) approaches, as well as new ones corresponding to the Russell measures, the directional distance function, DDF (including novel extensions like the reverse DDF, modified DDF, or generalizations based on Hölder norms), the generalized distance function, and additive measures like the slack based measure, the weighted additive distance function, etc. Moreover, regardless the underlying economic efficiency model, many of these technical inefficiency measures are available for calculation in a computer software for the first time. This article details the theoretical methods and the empirical implementation of the functions, comparing the obtained results using a common dataset on Taiwanese Banks.

detail.abstract: As organizational structures flatten, teams are increasingly granted decision autonomy with little to no hierarchical oversight. Prior research shows that team members can effectively use subjective peer information to curb free riding and motivate effort provision, if specific control mechanisms are in place. Yet, it is unclear whether teams should be granted decision autonomy over the very control mechanisms that coordinate the use of such peer information. To address this question, we conduct an experiment in which teams choose a mechanism to allocate a reward among members. Specifically, they can choose between an even-split mechanism, which may appear fair but enables free riding, and either of two peer-based mechanisms (i.e., bargaining or impartial sharing) that can limit free riding via the use of peer information. We find that both peer-based mechanisms increase effort provision by about 50 percent relative to even splits. However, when given a choice, most teams opt for even splits, foregoing the ability to confine free riding. As such, we provide evidence that teams select control mechanisms that are not in their own best interest. Our study reveals a key tension when delegating decision autonomy to teams: while granting autonomy over the use of subjective peer information is beneficial (i.e., helps) if specific control mechanisms are in place, granting autonomy over the very choice of control mechanism that coordinates the use of such peer information may backfire (i.e., hurts).

detail.title: Taming Cycles: China’s Growth Targets and Macroeconomic Management
detail.abstract: China’s hybrid economy blends state planning with market mechanisms, using annual economic targets to guide development and macroeconomic management to ensure their achievement. Local governments set ambitious growth targets to align with central mandates and incentivize subordinates, leading to asymmetric adjustments: targets rise rapidly during booms but decline sluggishly during slowdowns. This dynamic has heightened pressure on local governments to intervene in the economy, particularly after 2010. Our analysis shows that when a region falls short of its growth target, it increases infrastructure investment, land sales, and local government debt to close the gap. Notably, during the relatively stable period of 2011–2019, overly optimistic targets contributed an additional 14.0% of GDP to local government debt. While these interventions helped smooth cyclical fluctuations and moderated the trend of GDP deceleration, they also eroded GDP growth’s reliability as an economic indicator, weakening its correlation with corporate revenue, household demand, and TFP gains.

detail.abstract:
In her recent book on religions and development, Emma Tomalin asks the following questions: "Is religion negative for women's development and the pursuit of gender equality? Is there a gender consequence that results from engagement with religion?1 In an attempt to answer these questions, this chapter examines whether the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can empower a group of marginalised Buddhist women, sup- port them against existing power relations, and achieve integration over sources of power. Its premise is that the future of humanity rests on how development organizations can negotiate the rights of women in the religious sphere by providing support to women who ground their social work and activism in a religious framework. It suggests that in order to move forward with many new SDGs, including the elimination of poverty, as well as ensur- ing inclusive health and promoting well-being, quality education, gender equality and empowering women, reduced inequalities, peace, justice, and

strong institutions,"2 it is imperative to consider the many facets of religious contexts and the increased politicization of culture. The chapter argues for the importance of religious women in social development, a neglected area in development studies.

detail.abstract: The present analysis moves away from a traditional literature review to propose a global theoretical framework for racism that integrates its multiple dimensions: historical, colonial, biological, cultural, spiritual, and intersectional. Through the synthesis of a vast range of case studies-from educational policies in post-apartheid South Africa and racial ideologies in fascist Italy, to neoracism in Europe, the dynamics of racialization in Latin America, and the manifestations of Islamophobia and xenophobia globally-it is argued that racism is not a monolithic phenomenon, but a dynamic process of racialization. This process adapts and mutates, transitioning from explicit biologist discourses to more subtle but equally pernicious culturalist and differentialist forms. It is maintained that any global theory of racism must abandon Eurocentrism and recognize coloniality as its fundamental matrix, while also incorporating the intersectionality of race, class, and gender as an indispensable analytical element. It is concluded that racism operates through ideologically sustained mechanisms of dehumanization and is perpetuated through the construction of an other that is functional to power structures, whether in the Global North or the Global South.

This article explores the assignment markets with a moderator to ensure coordination and collaboration between buyers and sellers, examining the utility. The exercise of control involves an agent exerting control over other agents by fundamentally altering the utility. In this context, control represents the realization of an inherent capacity. To clarify, we distinguish between possessing control and actively exercising it. Possession refers to the latent capacity an agent holds while exercising control, which involves putting that capacity into action. We define and introduce the assignment market games under with moderator, and we study the core and the competitive equilibrium.

title: Dual shares, large owners, and corporate cash holdings
affiliations: Hanken School of Economics, HANKEN School of Economics, Hanken School of Economics and Swedish School of Economics and Business Administration

detail.title: Dual shares, large owners, and corporate cash holdings
detail.abstract: We contribute to the literature on the relation between the separation of voting and capital rights and corporate cash holdings. We use detailed ownership data for firms in the Nordic countries, where shareholder rights are strong, ownership concentration often high, and the large owners typically poorly diversified. We find that dual-class shares in association with high voting rights of the largest owner is associated with significantly lower corporate cash holdings. Our results cannot be explained by corporate cash being valued lower in dual-class firms due to agency problems, or by a precautionary motive. As dual shares facilitate a better portfolio diversification (less capital needed for given control rights in terms of votes), a potential explanation may come from the largest owner’s diversification needs. We find some support for this in terms of a significant positive relationship between the firm’s weight in the portfolio of the largest owner, and corporate cash.

title: From Ideologies to Practice: A Political Ecology Approach to Green Transitions–The Case of Tanzania’s Ujamaa Sustainability Communities

detail.title: From Ideologies to Practice: A Political Ecology Approach to Green Transitions–The Case of Tanzania’s Ujamaa Sustainability Communities
detail.abstract: Sustainable living is a core construct within the global green movement. Envisioning a more environmentally conscious future for Earth, the green movement denounces high consumption lifestyles and fossil fuel dependence. Like other nations, African countries are increasingly joining the green movement by trying to pursue lowcarbon growth and sustainable development. So far, this green transition has been easier said than done. For the most part, capacity gaps and non-compliance among local populations and special interest groups within countries persist for various reasons. Green transitions thus constitute a complex meshwork of ideologies, policies, and practices that need further exploration in the development literature. Whereas previous studies have focused on the econometrics of green transitions, this study takes a political ecology approach. Utilizing a qualitative historical case study and content analysis, this article examines key factors that impact the realization of this proposed green future for the African continent. The historical case analyzed is the Ujamaa policy and communities (Ujamaa Villages) established by the government of Tanzania between 1967 and 1985. The findings of this study suggest that despite the promise of a more just, sustainable, and eco-friendly future, embedded colonial legacies, hypercapitalist markets, and neoliberal values often undermine the implementation of programs and projects that are needed to jump-start and maintain green transitions, particularly in natural resourcedependent post-colonial societies. Shaped by these ideological and socio-ecological paradoxes, government interests, media portrayals, and public choices are often antagonistic to sustainability practices. This article further highlights the intricate interplay between political ideology, development economics, social-environmental movements, and land use ecology in Africa and the wider Global South.

detail.title: Mitigating Economic Losses and Prospects for the Development of the Energy Sector in the Republic of Kosovo
detail.abstract: The purpose of the study was to analyse the current economic problems in the energy sector of Kosovo and to develop effective strategies to overcome them, in particular ways to minimise losses and increase the stability of the energy system, as well as to study opportunities for ensuring the country's long-term development and energy security. The main focus was on the economic impact of implementing international energy standards, particularly European ones, within Kosovo's national policy and development strategy. The analysis emphasised the financial benefits and challenges associated with aligning the country's energy sector with EU directives, especially those related to renewable energy sources and energy efficiency. Key areas of the study included the economic potential of enhancing energy security, promoting renewable energy development, and reducing reliance on fossil fuels. Additionally, the study evaluated the economic implications of these reforms on Kosovo's energy market and overall economic growth trajectory. The study also included an economic analysis that assessed possible economic losses associated with the transition to renewable energy sources. Risks were considered, including job losses in traditional energy sectors such as coal and the significant financial costs required to upgrade infrastructure. However, the study found that the long-term benefits of a green energy transition, including increased energy security, reduced dependence on energy imports and improved environmental conditions, outweigh the short-term economic costs. The results showed that although the economic transition is accompanied by significant financial costs, the long-term benefits, such as increased energy security and reduced emissions, are substantial. The study highlights the importance of further reforms and investments to ensure the sustainable development of Kosovo’s energy sector, as well as the country’s integration into the European energy environment.

title: The Pandemic, Gender, and Work Productivity Evidence from the Real Estate Brokerage Industry
affiliations: University of Alabama,  and University of Central Florida

detail.title: The Pandemic, Gender, and Work Productivity Evidence from the Real Estate Brokerage Industry
detail.abstract: We study the effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on real estate agent work productivity, highlighting differences between male and female agents. We show that relative to male counterparts, female listing agent performance is more adversely affected by the pandemic. The loss of productivity is greater for women with fewer years of experience, who are more likely to be part-timers or parents with school-age children. The results are robust across alternative specifications and matched sample analysis. The empirical evidence is consistent with a family division of labor in which women bear a greater proportion of the burden of domestic work and childcare. This division of labor compromises women’s job productivity and reduces compensation - effects magnified by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Authoritarianism and the Next Generation: Evidence from Taiwan's Classroom Randomization
affiliations: Anhui University, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Anhui University

detail.title: Authoritarianism and the Next Generation: Evidence from Taiwan's Classroom Randomization
detail.abstract: Existing work underestimates how authoritarian educational legacies transmit intergenerationally through both direct familial channels and classroom peer effects. Drawing on longitudinal data, we identify three core direct consequences of maternal exposure to authoritarian peda-gogy: significant declines in children's academic performance, mea-surable deterioration in cognitive development, and increased engage-ment in risk-taking behaviors. These effects operate through disrupted noncognitive skill formation and emotionally detached parenting prac-tices, persisting uniformly across socioeconomic groups. The analysis further reveals two critical spillover effects within classrooms: peer-mediated declines in cognitive ability and depressed academic achieve-ment among classmates, particularly in under-resourced learning en-vironments. Long-term tracking demonstrates these dual transmis-sion pathways-direct familial and indirect peer-based-consolidate into durable deficits in educational and professional trajectories. The findings challenge assumptions that institutional democratization au-tomatically dissolves historically embedded inequities, highlighting in-stead the need for targeted interventions addressing both household dy-namics and peer learning environments to break self-reinforcing cycles of disadvantage.

title: From Childhood Adversity to Adolescent Motherhood: A Cross-Sectional Study of Trauma, Partner Age Gaps, and Parenting in the Dominican Republic
affiliations: Tulane University - School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine and Universidad Iberoamericana

detail.title: From Childhood Adversity to Adolescent Motherhood: A Cross-Sectional Study of Trauma, Partner Age Gaps, and Parenting in the Dominican Republic
detail.abstract: Background: Adolescent pregnancy increasingly represents a consequence rather than a cause of disadvantage, yet critical gaps remain regarding which adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) predict early childbearing, partner characteristics, and parenting trajectories. Objective: To examine associations among ACEs, partner characteristics, and parenting practices in adolescent versus adult-onset mothers. Participants and Setting: We recruited 1,019 mothers of children aged 24–48 months from poverty-focused programs in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic (November 2024–January 2025). Mothers were classified as current adolescent (<20 years, n=91), former adolescent (first birth <20, now ≥20, n=316), or adult-onset (first birth ≥20, n=598). Methods: Data collected via Audio Computer-Assisted Self-Interview using validated instruments: ACE questionnaire, HITS violence screen, Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, and standardized parenting assessments. Analyses included ANOVA, chi-square, and regression. Results: Early childbearing was associated with emotional neglect (50·2% vs 34·2% for <18 vs ≥30; p=0·005), physical neglect (50·7% vs 34·2%; p=0·018), and family incarceration (22·9% vs 12·7%; p=0·034). Minor adolescent mothers had partners 9·1 years older versus 2·5 years for mothers ≥26 (p<0·001, η²=0·089), with lower education (40·4% primary-only vs 13·0%). Emotional neglect predicted older partners (β=-1·65, p<0·01). Former adolescent mothers used less violent discipline than adult-onset mothers (-0·15 vs 0·07; p=0·001, d=-0·23). Conclusions: Adolescent motherhood reflects accumulated adversity transmitted intergenerationally through partner relationships. Yet, former adolescent mothers demonstrate adaptive parenting practices, supporting strengths-based interventions addressing childhood trauma.​

title: Temporal Deterrence: Response Velocity and Threshold Stability in NATO Airspace, 2022-2025
affiliations: University of Tehran - Faculty of Law and Political Sciences

detail.title: Temporal Deterrence: Response Velocity and Threshold Stability in NATO Airspace, 2022-2025
detail.abstract: Historical patterns demonstrate that accommodating territorial violations through delayed or absent responses systematically erodes deterrent thresholds, inviting escalation regardless of eventual diplomatic action. European accommodation of incremental German boundary violations between 1936–1938 cumulatively undermined deterrence until continental war became inevitable. Russia's 2014 Crimea annexation, met with economic sanctions but no military response, preceded systematic escalation culminating in full-scale Ukraine invasion eight years later. Conversely, Turkey's immediate 2015 shoot-down of a violating Russian aircraft produced economic retaliation but no military escalation spiral, validating decisive territorial defense. This article refines classical deterrence theory by explicitly operationalizing the temporal dimension—response velocity—that existing frameworks have underspecified despite its strategic significance. Building on Boyd's OODA loop insights and recent gray-zone literature, this analysis extends temporal considerations by: (1) formalizing threshold erosion mechanisms in sovereignty violations specifically, (2) developing standardized measurement tools (Violation Intensity Index), and (3) proposing graduated operational protocols (Escalation-Resistant Air Defense) that balance speed with escalation control. Three mechanisms formalize this dynamic: Threshold Erosion Dynamics (how inadequate response velocity enables normalization), Credibility Cascade Effects (how weakness propagates across security domains), and Graduated Response Calibration (how immediate proportionate action preserves escalation control while delayed responses invite threshold migration). Between February 2022 and September 2025, Russian forces violated NATO sovereign airspace on at least 35 documented occasions. The September 2025 sequence—Poland's immediate drone neutralization, Estonia's delayed fighter intercept, Denmark's persistent infrastructure targeting—provides contemporary illustration consistent with theoretical expectations. However, these recent cases serve as examples consonant with historical patterns rather than independent causal proof given limited temporal depth and numerous confounding variables. Two operational instruments—the Violation Intensity Index (VII) for standardized assessment and Escalation-Resistant Air Defense (ERAD) protocols for graduated response—translate theory into testable practice. The analysis draws primarily on comparative historical evidence spanning multiple contexts while employing rigorous methodological standards distinguishing sovereign airspace violations from routine international intercepts. Implications extend to democratic legitimacy within European societies and alliance cohesion dynamics.

AI.tldr: 本文通过分析历史案例（1936-1938年德国边界侵犯、2014年克里米亚吞并、2015年土耳其击落俄罗斯战机）和当代案例（2022-2025年俄罗斯侵犯北约领空），提出并完善了威慑理论中的时间维度——响应速度，认为及时、适度的领土防御能有效防止威慑阈值侵蚀和冲突升级。
AI.research_question: 响应速度如何影响领土侵犯中的威慑效果和冲突升级动态？
AI.motivation: 现有威慑理论对时间维度（响应速度）的规范不足，尽管历史模式表明延迟或缺失的应对会系统性侵蚀威慑阈值，导致冲突升级。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于经典威慑理论、博伊德的OODA循环理论和灰色地带文献，构建了包含阈值侵蚀动态、可信度级联效应和分级响应校准的理论框架。
AI.method: 采用比较历史分析方法，跨越多个情境，并运用严格的方法论标准区分主权领空侵犯与常规国际拦截。
AI.findings: 及时、适度的领土防御（如土耳其2015年击落俄罗斯战机）能有效防止冲突升级，而延迟或不足的响应（如欧洲对德国1936-1938年侵犯的绥靖、对2014年克里米亚吞并的经济制裁）会导致威慑阈值侵蚀和系统性升级。
AI.theory_contributions: 明确操作化了威慑理论中的时间维度（响应速度），形式化了主权侵犯中的阈值侵蚀机制，并提出了标准化测量工具（侵犯强度指数）和分级操作协议（抗升级防空）。
AI.practical_contributions: 开发了侵犯强度指数（VII）用于标准化评估，以及抗升级防空（ERAD）协议用于分级响应，将理论转化为可测试的实践，对欧洲社会的民主合法性和联盟凝聚力具有启示。
